correctness.rationale: In skew forcing the color of the forcing vertex is irrelevant, so on a bipartite graph each shore evolves using only its own white set and the opposite-shore neighborhoods as tests. The whole forcing family is a product. For an independent exact check I enumerated inclusion-minimal white stopping sets on both shores of each stated graph and then checked all black seeds against those sets: a stopping set cannot lose its first white vertex, and any nonempty stalled residual white set contains a minimal stopping set. This reproduced every coefficient of both factors and the forbidden triples, including the Pappus shore permutation and the extra parallel class. For Desargues no addition across black components is possible and two-edge paths successively shorten to edges, so closure fills the complete graphs on the initial components; complementation gives the other shore. The connected-graph recurrence and the exact finite check agree. The explicit basis-exchange axiom was checked for all minimum shore seeds, and the identified bases are those of the displayed geometric, sparse-paving and graphic matroids. An exchange from any current basis toward a target basis decreases the difference by one, proving the distance formula. Each whole optimum has the shore minimum on each side, so jumping gives a Cartesian square and sliding across a bipartition never preserves optimality. The one-shore edge counts 126, 300, 540, 930 and eccentricity counts 28, 48, 72 at 3 and (5 at 3, 120 at 4) for Desargues reproduce the table and whole Desargues eccentricity counts 25, 1,200, 14,400. For the Desargues eccentricities, a disconnected complement of a tree requires all edges of a cut in the tree; a 2-versus-3 cut needs six edges, so only a star has disconnected complement. Its complement is K_4 plus one isolated vertex and there is a spanning tree using just one star edge. No assumption on probabilistic seeds or on extrapolation is needed.
residual_risks: The comment at frozen verify.py lines 88–89 overstates a converse: realizing the Hamming lower bound in a Johnson subgraph does not by itself establish a matroid basis family (e.g. {12,23,34} is an isometric path but violates basis exchange). The theorem uses the actual matroid descriptions, and the independent check verifies the basis axiom explicitly; the false converse is not used.
Certification is for the four labelled graph models and ordinary skew forcing only.

value.rationale: These are standard exceptional cubic incidence examples, and their minimum forcing sets are relevant to reconfiguration under both a global edit and a graph-local one. The result is not just another minimum cardinality table: it identifies the obstruction geometry, recovers the missing affine direction in the Pappus case, and explains why minimum sets are slide-frozen but have exact shortest jump paths, with a separate metric profile for the graphic case. The full forcing polynomials distinguish behavior beyond minima. The finite checks cover the natural complete families on these four graphs rather than a selected subset of seeds.
residual_risks: The result supplies a four-object classification, not a general bipartite skew-forcing matroid theorem. Some component formulas are routine once the object-specific identification is made.
